description: We are AstroNex 🚀, interested in space science, web development, and data analysis. We aim to develop a wildfire monitoring solution using NASA satellite data. We welcome teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, data science, and UI/UX design. Let's innovate together!
summary:
Project Summary

We are developing a web-based platform that harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS satellite active fire hotspot data to create a unified Burning Activity Calendar. The application integrates historical fire observations spanning more than two decades and processes them into a consistent format for meaningful comparison and analysis. Users can explore fire activity through interactive maps, calendar-based heatmaps, historical trends, and regional analytics. The platform also identifies unusual increases in burning activity and highlights recurring high-risk periods by comparing current observations with historical patterns.

By addressing differences in satellite sensors, spatial resolutions, and detection characteristics, our solution aims to provide a more consistent understanding of global burning activity, including wildfires and agricultural burns. This platform can support emergency responders, scientists, and land managers in monitoring fire patterns, anticipating critical periods, improving preparedness, and making more informed decisions for fire management and environmental protection.
details: Project Details – Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hotspots 1. What does the project do and how does it work? Our project is a web-based platform designed to harmonize active fire hotspot data collected by NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors. It integrates historical satellite observations spanning more than two decades into a consistent dataset for analyzing global burning activity, including wildfires and agricultural burns. The system collects hotspot data from NASA FIRMS, processes and cleans the datasets, standardizes their temporal and spatial information, and applies harmonization techniques to address differences between the satellite sensors. The processed data is presented through an interactive map, a burning activity calendar, historical trend charts, and regional analytics. Users can select an area of interest, explore historical burning patterns, compare different time periods, and identify unusual increases in fire activity. 2. What are the benefits? - Combines MODIS and VIIRS observations into a more consistent analytical dataset. - Provides access to historical burning activity patterns. - Helps identify seasonal burning trends and critical periods. - Highlights unusual changes in hotspot activity. - Makes complex satellite data easier to understand through interactive visualizations. - Supports better monitoring and data-driven decision-making. 3. What is the intended impact? Our goal is to support emergency responders, scientists, environmental researchers, and land managers by providing a better understanding of when and where burning activity occurs. The platform aims to improve fire monitoring, help identify periods of unusually high burning activity, support early preparedness, and contribute to more informed fire management strategies. It can also help researchers study long-term changes in global burning patterns and their environmental implications. 4. What tools, programming languages, and software are used? Frontend: - React.js - HTML5 - CSS3 - JavaScript - Tailwind CSS Backend: - Python - FastAPI Data Processing and Analysis: - Pandas - NumPy - GeoPandas Database: - PostgreSQL - PostGIS Data Visualization and Mapping: - Leaflet.js - Recharts Machine Learning and Analysis: - Scikit-learn Data Source: - NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) - MODIS and VIIRS active fire datasets The platform uses satellite datasets and software-based data processing; no specialized physical hardware is required for the proposed system. 5. How is the project creative and innovative? The innovative aspect of our project is transforming fragmented satellite fire observations into a unified, interactive burning activity calendar. Instead of simply displaying individual satellite hotspots, our platform focuses on harmonizing observations, revealing long-term patterns, and making historical comparisons easier. The combination of: - A unified MODIS and VIIRS data analysis approach. - An interactive geographical burning activity calendar. - Historical and seasonal pattern analysis. - Unusual burning activity detection. - Region-specific insights. creates a more accessible way to explore satellite-based fire information and understand changes in burning activity over time. 6. What factors did our team consider? During the design of the project, we considered: - Differences in spatial resolution and detection capabilities between MODIS and VIIRS. - Data quality, confidence levels, and possible duplicate observations. - Consistent spatial and temporal aggregation. - Historical data availability and sensor coverage periods. - Usability and accessibility for different types of users. - Accuracy and reliability of analytical results. - Scalability to support different geographical regions. - The importance of distinguishing unusual hotspot activity from confirmed wildfire emergencies. We designed the project with the aim of making complex satellite observations more understandable, comparable, and useful for real-world environmental monitoring and decision-making.
